title: Minimum Time to Break Locks I
statement:
There are `n` locks, and lock `i` can be broken once the sword's energy is at least `strength[i]`. The sword starts with energy `0` and a growth factor `x = 1`; at the end of every minute its energy rises by `x`. Locks are broken one at a time, in any order you choose: as soon as the energy reaches the strength of the lock you are working on, that lock breaks, the energy drops back to `0`, and `x` grows by `k`.

Return the fewest minutes in which all `n` locks can be broken.
notes:
## Intuition

With factor `x`, the energy after `t` minutes is `t · x`, so a lock of strength `s` takes `ceil(s / x)` minutes. The next lock's factor depends only on how many locks are already broken (`1 + broken · k`), so the total depends only on the order. With at most 8 locks there are at most 8! = 40,320 orders: try them all with backtracking, abandoning a partial order once it is no faster than the best complete one.

## Approach

1. `search(broken, time)` extends a partial order: `broken` locks are open after `time` minutes, and `used` marks which ones.
2. If `time >= best`, stop: finishing this order cannot beat `best`.
3. If all `n` locks are broken, this order is the fastest so far: `best = time`.
4. Otherwise the factor is `1 + broken * k`. For each unused lock `i`, mark it, recurse with `time + ceil(strength[i] / factor)`, then unmark it.
5. Call `search(0, 0)` and return `best`.

## Example 1, step by step

`strength = [3, 4, 1]`, `k = 1`. The first full order, locks 0, 1, 2, takes `3 + ceil(4/2) + ceil(1/3) = 3 + 2 + 1 = 6` minutes, so `best = 6`. Every other order that starts with lock 0 or lock 1 also reaches 6 and is dropped. Starting with lock 2 costs 1 minute; lock 0 then lock 1 adds `ceil(3/2) + ceil(4/3) = 2 + 2`, total 5. Lock 1 then lock 0 adds `ceil(4/2) + ceil(3/3) = 2 + 1`, total 4, the answer.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n · n!) in the worst case: up to n! orders, each step scanning `n` locks; pruning usually skips much of it.
- Space: O(n) for `used` and the recursion depth.

## Pitfalls

- A lock takes `ceil(strength / factor)` minutes; a partial last minute still counts in full.
- The factor depends on how many locks are already broken, not on the lock's index.
- Weakest first is not always optimal: for `strength = [27, 29, 20]`, `k = 4`, the order 20, 29, 27 takes 29 minutes but 20, 27, 29 takes 30.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `used` | which locks the current partial order has broken |
| `best` | the least total time of any complete order found so far |
| `broken` | how many locks the partial order has broken |
| `time` | minutes the partial order has taken |
| `factor` | the sword's growth factor for the next lock |
| `i` | the lock tried next |

narration.3: used marks the locks the current partial order has already broken.
narration.4: best is the fastest complete order found so far; none yet.
narration.6: search extends a partial order that has broken some locks in time minutes.
narration.7: Already no faster than the best complete order: finishing this one cannot help.
narration.9: ...and faster than any earlier order, so remember this time.
narration.12: The sword's factor grows by k for each lock already broken.
narration.13: Try each lock as the next one to break.
narration.14: Skip locks this order has already broken.
narration.16: Breaking it takes ceil(strength[i] / factor) minutes; continue the order from there.
narration.17: Undo the choice so the next branch can use lock i later.
narration.21: Start with no locks broken and no time spent.
narration.22: The least total time over all orders.
